newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end higher, power sector shines.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end higher, power sector shines.

text.p: Stretching their winning streak to four sessions, Chilean blue chips closed sharply higher in heavy trade with the market still led by heavyweight electricity shares, said traders.
The rally is seen petering out next week as investors focus on second quarter results, they said.
"I think the market will be flat, except for specific stocks moving in reaction to earnings," said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investment.
The weighted index closed up 1.33 percent at 134.62 points, bring the rise for the week to 3.5 percent.
The general index firmed 0.54 percent to 5,737.13 points amid turnover of 20.7 billion pesos.
Traders reported the Enersis group continued to be buoyed by media reports of better-than-expected second quarter earnings.
Enersis closed up 1.49 percent at 306 pesos with subsidiary Endesa rising 1.58 percent to 322 pesos.
Another power giant, Chilgener, rallied on news that its shareholders had bought all the stock offered in a $500 million rights issue, they said.
"The placement is very important as it shows the company will not have problems funding future projects," said Tagle.
Chilgener, Chile's second largest generator, ended up 1.42 percent at 178 pesos.
Losers included vineyard San Pedro, down 2.72 percent at 3.5 pesos, and bottler Andina, which shed 1.96 percent to 1,500 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
